help.title: Help — {context}
help.guide.step1.heading: What is Cadence?
help.guide.step1.1: Cadence uses spaced repetition: you review each item just before your brain forgets it, so you retain it durably with a minimum of reviews.
help.guide.step1.2: The more regularly you review, the longer the interval grows — and the less effort learning takes.
help.guide.step1.3: Each item to learn becomes a "card": a tune, a word, a concept, etc.
help.guide.step1.4: Cards are grouped into decks that you can review independently.
help.guide.step2.heading: Create your first card
help.guide.step2.1: Click the "+" button in the top right of the Library to create a card.
help.guide.step2.2: Give it a name, then open the card to add notes, files or links.
help.guide.step2.3: Tip: if you're learning tunes from TheSession, use the dedicated import to bring them in with their ABC notation in one click!
help.guide.step3.heading: Organise into decks
help.guide.step3.1: A deck is a group of cards to study together (e.g. "Jazz", "Folk songs", "Spanish vocabulary").
help.guide.step3.2: Create a deck using the dedicated button in the sidebar, then add cards to it.
help.guide.step3.3: Add a card to a deck from the Library, or directly when creating it.
help.guide.step3.4: A card can belong to multiple decks — handy for cross-referencing themes!
help.guide.step4.heading: Start a study session
help.guide.step4.1: Click "Study" on any deck to begin reviewing.
help.guide.step4.2: The app only shows cards that need reviewing right now, to avoid unnecessary repetition.
help.guide.step4.3: If no cards are available, come back later: your brain is consolidating right now!
help.guide.step5.heading: Rate yourself honestly
help.guide.step5.1: Again: you didn't remember. The card comes back very soon.
help.guide.step5.2: Hard: you remembered, but it was a struggle. The card will come back fairly soon.
help.guide.step5.3: Good: you remembered correctly. The next review is pushed back.
help.guide.step5.4: Easy: it was obvious! The app will wait much longer before showing it again.
help.guide.step6.heading: Track your progress
help.guide.step6.1: The home page is a dashboard: it gives you an estimate of what you currently have mastered.
help.guide.step6.2: Check a deck's page to see its overall metrics and the status of each card.
help.guide.step6.3: Click on a card to see its individual metrics in detail: recall, stability, ease.
help.home.welcome.heading: What is Cadence?
help.home.welcome.1: Cadence is a spaced repetition tool — it helps you learn and retain anything over time by showing you what to review at exactly the right moment.
help.home.welcome.2: Create cards for what you want to learn, group them in decks, and review regularly. Cadence handles the scheduling.
help.home.welcome.3: The more consistently you review, the better the algorithm models your memory — and the less time you need to maintain what you know.
help.home.nav.heading: Why spaced repetition works
help.home.nav.1: Reviewing something just before you're likely to forget it strengthens the memory far more than reviewing it while it's still fresh.
help.home.nav.2: Short, consistent sessions beat long, infrequent ones — 10 minutes a day outperforms an hour once a week.
help.home.nav.3: Well-reviewed cards are shown less and less often — knowledge gradually moves into long-term memory.
help.home.organize.heading: Dashboard & organizing
help.home.organize.1: The dashboard shows your stats and an activity graph — click a bar, or shift-click a range, to see how many sessions happened then.
help.home.organize.2: Star a deck to pin it in the Favorites row at the top of the home page.
help.home.organize.3: Drag folders and decks to reorder them, or drop one folder onto another to nest it inside.
help.home.organize.4: "Study all" studies every card in the current folder and its subfolders at once.
help.folder.what.heading: What is a folder?
help.folder.what.1: A folder groups related decks together. It's purely organisational and doesn't affect the learning algorithm.
help.folder.what.2: Folders can be nested inside other folders to build any hierarchy that suits your needs.
help.folder.what.3: Click the folder icon in the sidebar to expand or collapse it. Drag folders and decks to reorganise them.
help.folder.actions.heading: Managing this folder
help.folder.actions.1: Click the folder's name to rename it.
help.folder.actions.2: "Location" shows the current parent folder — click it to move this folder somewhere else instantly.
help.folder.actions.3: Deleting a folder removes it and everything inside it; you'll be offered the option to also delete any cards that would end up in no deck at all as a result.
help.library.browse.heading: What is the library?
help.library.browse.1: The library is the master list of all your cards, across all decks. A card can belong to multiple decks simultaneously.
help.library.browse.2: Each card shows two dots: recall score (red/yellow/green) and ease. These reflect your review history.
help.library.browse.3: Use the library to search, filter by tag or deck, and manage cards independently of any particular deck.
help.library.browse.4: Cards deleted here are permanently removed from all decks. Removing a card from a deck (via the deck view) only unlinks it.
help.library.tools.heading: Sorting, selecting & adding cards
help.library.tools.1: Sort by name, last studied, date added, importance, recall or ease — click the sort button again to reverse the order.
help.library.tools.2: The card map (top-right icon) plots your cards visually — position reflects recall and stability.
help.library.tools.3: Select multiple cards (checkboxes, or shift-click a range) to study, export, move between decks, or delete them all at once.
help.library.tools.4: "New card" lets you create one by hand, import from TheSession/IrishTuneInfo, generate cards with an AI assistant, or restore a shared/exported package.
help.deck.study.heading: What is a deck?
help.deck.study.1: A deck is a collection of cards you study together.
help.deck.study.2: A card can belong to multiple decks simultaneously — organise the same material in different ways without duplicating anything.
help.deck.study.3: When you study a deck, only cards whose recall score has dropped below your threshold are shown.
help.deck.manage.heading: Study strategies & importance
help.deck.manage.1: The three study strategies differ in how they prioritise cards. Each is described in the strategy picker on the deck page.
help.deck.manage.2: Importance is a weight that determines how often a card is prioritised relative to others in Optimal and Stochastic modes.
help.deck.manage.3: Each card has a base importance. Inside a deck, you can override this with a deck-specific value that only affects that deck.
help.deck.manage.4: Click the ×N value next to a card to edit its importance for this deck only. Drag cards to reorder the list.
help.deck.bar.heading: Deck metrics
help.deck.bar.1: Recall: average probability of recalling a card right now. Drops over time without review.
help.deck.bar.2: Stability: how long memories last before dropping below threshold. Grows with each successful review.
help.deck.bar.3: Ease: how naturally cards are recalled on average. Reflects difficulty history.
help.deck.bar.4: Mastery (X/Y): cards currently above the recall threshold out of the total.
help.deck.location.heading: Location & quick actions
help.deck.location.1: Star a deck to pin it in the Favorites row on the home page.
help.deck.location.2: "Location" shows the current parent folder — click it to move this deck somewhere else instantly.
help.deck.location.3: "View in library" opens the library filtered to just this deck's cards.
help.deck.location.4: Use the search field next to the card list to link an existing card into this deck, or "+" to create/import a new one straight into it.
help.card.edit.heading: What is a card?
help.card.edit.1: A card represents one thing you want to learn — a tune, a concept, a word, anything with a name.
help.card.edit.2: Each card has tags (to categorise it), an importance score (to prioritise it), and optional attachments: notes, audio files, ABC notation, links.
help.card.edit.3: Cadence tracks your recall history for each card individually and uses the FSRS algorithm to decide when to show it next.
help.card.edit.4: A card is independent of any deck — it can be linked to multiple decks and removed from one without affecting the others.
help.card.manage.heading: Linking & organizing
help.card.manage.1: If a card was imported from TheSession or IrishTuneInfo, a coloured pin next to its name links back to the original page.
help.card.manage.2: Click the deck chips under the title to add or remove this card from decks.
help.card.manage.3: Click the importance value to switch between the card's base importance and a value specific to one of its decks.
help.card.manage.4: Click a tag to rename it everywhere it's used, or add new ones from the input field.
help.card.manage.5: Add a file, a link (video, webpage…), or a reference to another card via the attachment bar below the notes — drag to reorder, hover and click ✕ to remove one.
help.card.fsrs.heading: Memory metrics
help.card.fsrs.1: Recall: the probability you can recall this card right now. Decays over time, resets upward after each review.
help.card.fsrs.2: Stability: how long the memory lasts. Grows with each successful recall — especially with Easy ratings.
help.card.fsrs.3: Ease: how naturally the card comes to you. Built from your difficulty history — improves as the card becomes more familiar.
help.card.notes.heading: Notes & hidden text
help.card.notes.1: Notes support Markdown: **bold**, *italics*, lists, links, tables, code…
help.card.notes.2: Wrap text in double pipes to hide it: ||like this||. It shows as an opaque pill — click to reveal, click again to hide.
help.card.notes.3: Perfect for question/answer cards: put the answer in a spoiler and it stays hidden during study (and in the notes preview) until you click it.
help.card.abc.heading: ABC files
help.card.abc.1: Click an .abc attachment to open the viewer: a Partition tab with a playback cursor, and a raw ABC tab you can edit and save.
help.card.abc.2: If the file contains multiple tunes, use the version switcher next to the tabs to navigate between them.
help.card.abc.3: Pick an instrument from the dropdown to change the sound used for playback.
help.card.history.heading: Review history
help.card.history.1: Click "+" in the review history to manually log a past session.
help.card.history.2: Hover an entry and click ✕ to remove it.
help.study.launch.heading: Before you start
help.study.launch.1: Context restricts the pool to cards shared with another deck, and uses that deck's importance overrides instead of the default ones.
help.study.launch.2: "Weight by importance" and "Exclude mastered" toggle whether importance and mastery affect which cards you see.
help.study.launch.3: Random, Optimal and Stochastic strategies differ in how they pick the next card — see the description under each one in the picker.
help.study.rating.heading: How studying works
help.study.rating.1: Cadence shows you cards whose recall score has dropped below your threshold — the ones you're most likely to have forgotten.
help.study.rating.2: After recalling a card, rate how easily it came to you. This is the key input the algorithm uses to schedule the next review.
help.study.rating.3: The harder it was to recall, the sooner the card will come back. The easier, the longer before you see it again.
help.study.rating.4: Be honest with your ratings — the algorithm works best when they reflect your actual recall.
help.study.shortcuts.heading: Rating scale
help.study.shortcuts.1: ✗ Again — no recall. The card resets and will reappear soon.
help.study.shortcuts.2: △ Hard — recalled with significant effort. Interval grows slowly.
help.study.shortcuts.3: ○ Good — correct recall with reasonable effort. Standard progression.
help.study.shortcuts.4: ✓ Easy — instant, effortless recall. Longest interval increase.
help.study.fsrs.heading: Tips
help.study.fsrs.1: You don't need to review everything — Cadence will only show cards that need it. Trust the scheduler.
help.study.fsrs.2: Consistency matters more than session length. A few cards every day beats a large batch once a week.
help.study.fsrs.3: Cards above your recall threshold are skipped automatically — they don't need reviewing yet. Disable "Exclude mastered" in the study options to review everything anyway.
help.study.fsrs.4: Hidden text (||…||) in the notes appears as an opaque pill — click it to reveal the answer.
help.study.end.heading: End of session
help.study.end.1: "Done" means every available card in this pool has been reviewed for now — come back later.
help.study.end.2: "Mastered" means every card is currently above your recall threshold — nothing needs reviewing right now.
help.study.end.3: A warning banner appears if some cards were excluded because they don't match the chosen study context.
help.modules.what.heading: What's here
help.modules.what.1: Modules are specialized tools beyond the core deck/study flow.
help.modules.what.2: Right now: the tune analyzer, which records or imports audio and recognizes tunes automatically.
help.modules.what.3: A pulsing dot next to a module in this list means a recording is currently active in it.
help.modules.sessions.heading: Recording a session
help.modules.sessions.1: Start a live recording or import an audio file — tunes are detected automatically as they play.
help.modules.sessions.2: Pause and resume a live recording anytime with the pause button next to Stop.
help.modules.sessions.3: If a recording is interrupted (tab refresh, crash), it's recovered automatically the next time you open the library — nothing is lost up to that point.
help.modules.sessions.4: When a detected tune already has a card, you can log a review for it directly from the result, live or afterward.
help.sessions.recording.heading: Recording live
help.sessions.recording.1: Start records through your microphone; tunes are detected and shown automatically as they play.
help.sessions.recording.2: Pause/resume anytime — the clock, VU meter and detector all pause together.
help.sessions.recording.3: Adjust the pitch shift (−12/+12 semitones) if the session isn't tuned to standard pitch — detection recalibrates live.
help.sessions.recording.4: Pick which deck(s) new cards should join — the deck icon in the status bar opens the picker.
help.sessions.recording.5: If the app crashes or the tab reloads mid-recording, the session is recovered automatically next time you open this module.
help.sessions.import.heading: Importing a recording
help.sessions.import.1: Pick an existing audio file to analyze instead of recording live — same detection, pitch-shift and deck controls.
help.sessions.import.2: A progress bar tracks decoding and analysis; cancel anytime before it finishes.
help.sessions.results.heading: Working with detected tunes
help.sessions.results.1: The confidence badge shows how sure the detector is; click a tune's name to open its card, or TheSession if it's not in your library yet.
help.sessions.results.2: ▶ plays the detected excerpt; the notation icon shows a quick sheet-music preview when available.
help.sessions.results.3: Tap the heart to mark a tune you liked hearing — a personal note, unrelated to the card system.
help.sessions.results.4: "+" creates a card for a detected tune that doesn't have one yet, and links it to your chosen deck(s).
help.sessions.summary.heading: Reviewing a finished session
help.sessions.summary.1: The segment bar is colour-coded by confidence — click anywhere to jump the player there.
help.sessions.summary.2: Adjust a segment's start/end (±5s), merge it into the previous one, or delete it.
help.sessions.summary.3: Extract a segment as an MP3 and attach it directly to its card.
help.sessions.summary.4: Rename the session, edit its date, or "forget" its audio to save space — detected tunes and annotations stay either way.
help.sessions.summary.5: Share a session, with or without its audio, via a file or a temporary key — same mechanism as sharing cards.
